metadata.title: AquaShield AI - Community Health Knowledge Base
metadata.purpose: Educational and symptom-guidance content for the community chatbot. This is not a diagnostic tool.
metadata.disclaimer: Symptoms can have many causes. The chatbot must not diagnose a disease or replace a healthcare professional. For severe, rapidly worsening, or emergency symptoms, seek medical care immediately.

conditions.name: Cholera
conditions.description: An acute diarrhoeal infection caused by consuming food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae.
conditions.water_connection: Strongly associated with contaminated food or drinking water and inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene.
prevention: Wash hands with soap and water.
Follow local public-health guidance during outbreaks.
urgent_warning_signs: inability to drink or keep fluids down
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Do not tell the user they have cholera from symptoms alone. Explain that acute watery diarrhoea and dehydration can have several causes and recommend prompt medical evaluation when symptoms are severe or worsening.

conditions.name: Typhoid fever
conditions.description: A serious infection caused by Salmonella Typhi. It can spread when food or water is contaminated with faeces from an infected person or carrier.
conditions.water_connection: Can spread through drinking water or food contaminated with faeces, especially where sanitation is inadequate.
transmission: food handled by someone who did not wash their hands
prevention: Practice safe food and drinking-water habits.
Wash hands with soap and water.
Follow vaccination advice from qualified healthcare professionals.
urgent_warning_signs: persistent or high fever with significant illness
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Fever and gastrointestinal symptoms can occur in many illnesses. The chatbot should describe typhoid as one possible association rather than diagnosing it.

conditions.name: Hepatitis A
conditions.description: An inflammation of the liver caused by hepatitis A virus.
conditions.water_connection: The virus can spread through ingestion of contaminated food or water. Risk is associated with unsafe water, poor sanitation and poor hygiene.
transmission: direct contact with an infectious person
prevention: Wash hands carefully after using the toilet and before preparing food.
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Jaundice and digestive symptoms require proper medical assessment. Do not infer hepatitis A solely from symptoms.

conditions.name: Hepatitis E
conditions.description: An inflammation of the liver caused by hepatitis E virus.
conditions.water_connection: Primarily transmitted through the faecal-oral route, principally through contaminated drinking water.
prevention: Avoid drinking water that may be contaminated.
urgent_warning_signs: pregnancy with suspected hepatitis E symptoms
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Symptoms can overlap with other liver and infectious diseases. The chatbot must not diagnose hepatitis E. Suspected cases need professional assessment, with particular caution during pregnancy.

conditions.name: Acute diarrhoeal disease
conditions.description: Diarrhoea can result from many bacterial, viral and parasitic infections and from other causes. It is a symptom or syndrome rather than one specific disease.
conditions.water_connection: Unsafe drinking water, inadequate sanitation and poor hygiene can contribute to infectious diarrhoeal disease.
prevention: Wash hands with soap and water.
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Do not map diarrhoea directly to one disease. Ask about duration, severity, fever, blood in stool, vomiting, hydration and possible contaminated-water exposure.

conditions.name: Giardiasis
conditions.description: An intestinal infection caused by Giardia. It can spread through contaminated water, food, surfaces or objects.
conditions.water_connection: Exposure can occur after swallowing contaminated water, including untreated water from lakes, rivers, springs or shallow wells.
prevention: Wash hands with soap and water.
Boil or appropriately treat potentially contaminated water.
conditions.chatbot_guidance: Diarrhoea has many possible causes. Giardia should be presented only as one possible cause when exposure history is compatible. A healthcare provider may use stool testing for diagnosis.

rules.note: Symptoms alone cannot confirm the cause.
Several infections can cause this combination.
Exposure history can help guide questions but cannot establish a diagnosis.

global_safety_rules: Never state or imply that symptoms confirm a disease.
Use wording such as 'may be associated with' or 'can occur with'.
Ask about duration, severity, hydration, blood in stool, fever and relevant water/food exposure when appropriate.
Recommend professional medical evaluation when symptoms are severe, persistent, worsening, or concerning.
For emergency symptoms, advise immediate emergency medical care.
Do not recommend prescription medicines or antibiotics without a qualified clinician.
Keep medical education separate from the project's outbreak-risk score.
